$comment: Six category circuits: the original core followed by four variety families per band. Exact scenario identities and score targets are frozen in pool.json; enjoyment and mixed-author handovers require playtesting.

Dynamic Clicking.title: Read. Confirm. Commit.
Dynamic Clicking.description: Follow the movement into each shot. Read arcs beyond the apex and stay with multi-hit targets until the final click. Smooth transitions make the next target easier to read.

families.focus: Read the drift. Click on confirmation.
families.why: Pasu without Voltaic's cuts. Viscose's entry version with limited strafing for Novice, SuperbAim's Easy and standard cuts in the middle, and Pasu Reload Goated for Expert, which is smaller and uses a reload instead of accuracy scoring.

families.focus: Meet the path. Confirm the shot.
families.why: Targets on a fixed path, so it's more about timing than reading. Easy and Hard S1 are from Aimerz+ S1; Normal and Hard are the older S0 cuts.

families.focus: Read the full bounce, not just the apex.
families.why: Bouncing-target clicking from two authors. SuperbAim's BounceClick for the first two rungs, then Sparky's and rAim's Bounce 180, where the balls really bounce and a reload replaces the accuracy penalty. The order between the two authors hasn't been playtested.

families.focus: Read horizontal movement through the shot.
families.why: Targets strafe around you and move up and down, so it's wider than Pasu. psalmTS angelic click and Pasu Angelic, each with a larger-target cut below it.

families.focus: Stay with each target for all three clicks.
families.why: Repeated hits add the sustained target reading missing from one-shot clicking. Wide Easy introduces the task; Less Easy uses a faster timescale than the easy v2 cut; standard v2 removes timescaling; Wide opens the field. These are related community edits, not a measured equal-step progression. Expert width and mixed v2/v4 behaviour need playtesting.

families.focus: Follow the arc into a clean click.
families.why: Popcorn with a reload instead of accuracy scoring. rAim's Goated easy cut with double-size targets, then rAim Easy, Sparky's version where the bots bounce, and Goated rAim with 10% smaller bots for Expert.

families.focus: Catch the next head as it drifts into view.
families.why: Floating heads in a layered arena offer a shooting-gallery rhythm with depth changes. Viscose's Entry through Hard edits supply a coherent four-band progression without replacing the core Pasu and Popcorn tests.

families.focus: Hop between layers. Catch each passing dot.
families.why: Far moving dots at several vertical layers turn the run into a layered gallery. The Goated Easier, Medium, Hard and Expert edits retain the same scene while changing the challenge.

families.focus: Ride the wave from shot to shot.
families.why: SunClick and WaveClick add a timing-focused wave circuit with a repeatable rhythm. This is a mixed-release progression using Aimerz's Easy S1, Normal, Hard and Hard S1 cuts; its handovers need playtesting.

families.focus: One clean click per mover.
families.why: CatClick is graded by Viscose in all four of its tiers, Easier, Medium, Hard and Expert, so the family is one scenario's own four cuts with no handover between authors, and its two easier cuts carry some of the busiest boards in the pool. Its author description says nothing about the mechanic; the season files it where Viscose does, under dynamic clicking.

Precise Tracking.title: Stay connected.
Precise Tracking.description: Match the target through horizontal strafes, vertical travel and changing paths. Make clean corrections when contact breaks. Use an easier cut when you lose the movement; difficulty should leave room to learn.

families.focus: Match the long arc with steady contact.
families.why: SmoothBot Invincible Goated at every rung instead of Voltaic's Smoothbot: 75% speed, Easy, the standard version, then the smaller cut for Expert. The bot can't die, so the whole run is time on target.

families.focus: Settle into the strafe. Match its speed.
families.why: A dedicated horizontal centering test separates velocity matching from multidirectional control. Entry, Novice and Intermediate community cuts lead into the established no-strafes version. Apogee band names describe our progression, not the names of the source cuts. Exact target-size differences are not claimed; band handovers need playtesting.

families.focus: Recover cleanly. Settle back on target.
families.why: Aimerz+ PreciseTrack in place of PGT as the fine-correction test. Avasive's Easier cut for Novice, then Easy, Med and Hard from the Aimerz+ S1 set.

families.focus: Match the curve and its changing speed.
families.why: Smooth with no blinks, going by the scenario description. 55% speed, 75%, full speed, then Extra Small for Expert.

rungs: Smooth Your Vertical Altered POV Entry
Smooth Your Vertical Altered POV Easy v2
Smooth Your Vertical Altered POV Intermediate
Smooth Your Vertical Altered POV v2
families.focus: Stay connected through the rise and fall.
families.why: These four Altered POV cuts explicitly isolate vertical smoothness. They replace a second broad sphere-control test with an axis players can identify and practise directly. Entry, Easy, Intermediate and standard v2 are curated into four Apogee bands; difficulty spacing remains a playtest judgement.

families.focus: Keep contact through changing directions.
families.why: A small dot that jumps gently and flies around you at changing distance and speed. Viscose's entry cut, then rAim's Easy at 90%, rAim Easy and rAim. The sheets file the top rung under Control Tracking, which this season grades as Precise.

families.focus: Follow the bounce all the way to the corner.
families.why: The DVD-inspired moving target gives continuous tracking a recognizable screen-bounce motif. MASSIVE, Big, standard and Small keep the motion theme while reducing the target size.

families.focus: Trace the flower. Stay with each little turn.
families.why: The author's bee-collecting-pollen theme gives compact tracking a playful identity. Entry, Easier, standard and Hard keep the Flower motion across the four bands. The scenario name is not a requirement to change sensitivity.

families.focus: Cruise with the dot as it circles you.
families.why: A gently jumping dot flying around the player adds a flowing orbital chase. Viscose's Horizontal Entry, Easier, standard and Hard cuts expand the motion challenge while keeping the same visual theme.

families.focus: Stay on it, not near it.
families.why: waldoTS is one of the most-played tracking scenarios in the catalogue, with 3.7 million plays on its standard cut. Viscose grades its Novice, Intermediate, standard and Elite cuts as Easier, Medium, Hard and Expert, and AimSpeed grades the standard and Elite cuts too, so the progression is one scenario's own cuts.

Reactive Tracking.title: React, recover, settle.
Reactive Tracking.description: Watch the target, react to the change, then match its new movement. Stops and teleports join ground and air reads. If you start guessing turns or forcing the mouse, step down and rebuild clean contact.

families.focus: Read each strafe. React after the turn.
families.why: Sparky's Ground Plaza v3: six bots strafing on the ground at mixed lengths and distances. Easy, the standard version, OW with instant ground acceleration, then Thin for Expert.

families.focus: Follow the aerial change without guessing.
families.why: Air Voltaic Invincible 4: one invincible bot changing direction in the air, nothing to kill. Viscose grades Entry, Easier and Medium; the full version is Expert.

families.focus: Recover from the turn, then match speed.
families.why: Air Angelic from Astro's and Jade Palace's sheets. rAim's Biggest cut, Easier, rAim Easy, then the standard version, which both of them grade at their top tier.

families.focus: Read the next strafe. Keep corrections clean.
families.why: Targets that only dodge horizontally. CB StrafeTrack Easy is the entry, then Aimerz+ VGS Easy, Med and Hard. Mixes two authors: the CB entry isn't part of the VGS set.

families.focus: Stay with the leap and read its direction.
families.why: A target that leaps and strafes with mixed dodge profiles. wobin's Easier cut, then Aimerz+'s mid-range Leapstrafes Control Medium, then wobin's standard and Hard cuts. No sheet names a sub-skill for wobin's version, so putting it in Reactive is a judgement call.

rungs: Flicker Plaza rAim Easy Less Blinks
families.focus: Read the change. Reacquire, then settle.
families.why: Recovery replaces a third mixed-air test. Kindaclose introduces random acceleration, slowing and stops; the three Flicker Plaza cuts then challenge reacquisition after teleports. This is a deliberate change of mechanic between Novice and Intermediate, not a shared-bot speed ladder. Less Blinks provides the transition.

families.focus: Stay ready for the next strange turn.
families.why: Air Spectral's deliberately unusual Air movement adds a surprise-driven chase. Easy 85%, Easy, standard and Harder retain that theme. Its terse author description supports the unusual-motion intent, not a claim of measured enjoyment.

families.focus: Follow the aerial course through every phase.
families.why: Air Divine-style movement brings a longer aerial course into the season. Easy Slowed, Easy, No UFO and Harder progress from a slowed course to the full challenge; the final UFO handover needs playtesting.
rungs: Air CELESTIAL No UFO Easy Slowed

families.focus: Read each dodge before it happens.
families.why: Air Pure mixes bots with different dodge profiles in one air arena, so every target asks for a different read. Revosect's time-scored entry cut, six bots circling the player, leads into the Intermediate, standard and Hard cuts that Viscose and snakbox grade. The handover between the two editions needs playtesting.

families.focus: Stay close. Catch the reversal.
families.why: A close strafing opponent adds a grounded duel-like chase beside the aerial courses. Easy Thin, standard, Thin and Precise+ are a proposed progression; speed and size both change, so the first handover needs playtesting.
rungs: Close Fast Strafes Easy Invincible - Thin

Speed Switching.title: Find pace. Keep precision.
Speed Switching.description: Hold fire, land close and finish each target before transferring. Mix compact flicks, wide routes and shrinking targets. In practice, try a short speed burst on an easier cut; use complete runs for benchmark scores.

families.focus: Land close. Confirm. Chain the next flick.
families.why: Static dot switching without Voltaic's cuts. wobin's Easy, which leans on horizontal spawns, for Novice, AimSpeed's Entry, the 30% larger cut, then plain DotTS, which Aimerz+ SpeedTS and AimSpeed both grade at Hard.

families.focus: Land, finish, transfer. Hold your pace.
families.why: Large and standard range targets establish routing and clean transfers. Viscose Varied introduces progressively shrinking targets; rAim finishes with a smaller fixed-target challenge. Only the Advanced rung is an evolving task. This adapts the source routine's speed-to-precision idea across related variants without changing their native scoring or duration.

families.focus: Keep transfers fast and finishes clean.
families.why: Four flying targets, about a quarter second each. Here so the category isn't just size variants of one range. Elite S5 is the Expert rung.

families.focus: Find the next target before the pivot.
families.why: Aimerz+ pivoTS, a different switching pattern. The two Hard cuts are from different Aimerz+ releases (S0 and S1), and their order hasn't been playtested yet.

families.focus: Hold fire. Finish before transferring.
families.why: You hold fire on each target instead of tapping, and some cuts regen if you flick off early. The slow-kill option next to DotTS and EddieTS.

families.focus: Choose a route and finish each target.
families.why: Spherical bots moving slowly side to side, tracked briefly to kill. psalmTS Voltaic is the Advanced rung and VT psalmTS Advanced is Expert.

families.focus: Clear the room in fast bursts.
families.why: Stationary Vox targets reward route choice and rapid full-auto clears without movement reading. Jumbo, standard, Small and xxSmall turn the room into a four-band switching sprint.

families.focus: Pass from wave to wave without losing pace.
families.why: Smoothly drifting targets give switching a visible wave rhythm. Community Benchmarks' easy cut leads into Revosect Entry, Intermediate and standard. The cross-author first handover is provisional.

families.focus: Sweep the sky one target at a time.
families.why: Slow horizontal targets at several depths make a readable aerial switching gallery. Four published skyTS bands keep the movement predictable while increasing the target challenge.

families.focus: Burst through the pack. Find the next clear.
families.why: Low-FOV target switching concentrates the action into short, fast clears. Easy, NR, rAim and NR Small are a proposed cross-edit progression; the two middle releases need an in-game difficulty comparison.

Evasive Switching.title: Earn every transfer.
Evasive Switching.description: Flick in, match the movement and confirm the kill. Read the next target without abandoning this one. Regeneration tests clean finishes; varied arcs and strafes keep the task about reading, not memorising turns.

families.focus: Land on the moving target, then finish.
families.why: Target switching on Pasu-style floating bots. PureG's flick-focused version, then PureG's higher time-to-kill version, then Aimerz+'s wide-wall Pasu Switch and its regen cut for Expert. Two authors, and the order between them hasn't been playtested.

families.focus: Finish the moving target before you leave.
families.why: Regenerating targets reward committed tracking after the flick. Entry and Intermediate use shorter time to kill; Control asks for longer contact; Hard adds bouncing. These are different training demands, not just faster versions. Unlike the retained Smooth family, the Control bots wiggle rather than circle.

families.focus: Track the whole arc. Confirm the finish.
families.why: An accessible rAim entry leads to Aimerz+'s depth-changing mid-high arcs, then two regenerative bounce edits. The final two variants make incomplete contact costly instead of relying only on smaller Elite bots. They deliberately retain two useful Voltaic variants rather than an entire stock four-rung family. Cross-author handovers and regeneration difficulty need playtesting.

families.focus: Follow the jump through the final hit.
families.why: Jumping targets. CB JumpSwitch Easy (four jumping targets) first, then Aimerz+ hopTS Easy, Med and Hard. Mixes two authors.

families.focus: Stay on the circle until the target falls.
families.why: Small dots circling you, 0.5s to kill, and they regen fast if you come off them. Starts on the 30% Larger cut of the Hard version.

families.focus: Read the flight. Finish, then transfer.
families.why: Four flying targets, 50 hits each. The S5 FlyTS cuts, with Elite as the Expert rung.

families.focus: Stay on target until it drops.
families.why: domiSwitch targets carry 55 health and regenerate 0.3 seconds after damage stops, so leaving early costs the whole kill; Aimerz+, snakbox and Viscose file it under evasive switching. Viscose's Easier cut and the Easy and standard cuts lead into Avasive's edit for the top band, whose top score is the lowest of the four. That edition handover needs playtesting.

families.focus: Chase the bouncing crowd around the pentagon.
families.why: Five targets bounce across a pentagonal wall and each needs a short sustained burst to clear. This adds an arena-like switching loop with plenty of target choice. The four published Season 5 cuts provide exact variants for every band.

families.focus: Clear the floating pack, one target at a time.
families.why: Four gently jumping and floating targets share a narrow chamber, producing a compact clear-the-room loop. The four published ControlTS bands keep the same arena and short sustained bursts throughout the progression.

families.focus: Flow into the next moving target.
families.why: Smooth transfer adds longer flowing target-to-target routes beside the sharper evasive circuits. Community Benchmarks' easy cut leads into Revosect's three SmoothTS tiers. The first cross-author handover needs playtesting.

Static Clicking.title: Still targets. Time between kills.
Static Clicking.description: Targets stationary. Score = gap between kills. One large initial flick → one small micro-correction → click. Straight line target to target, no overflick. During micro, next target already located in peripheral.

families.focus: Two targets. Flick → micro → click.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Diagonal path. Straight line, no curve.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Horizontal only. Flat line, time switch.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Tiny targets. Micro-correct, no overflick.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Small, rushed. Micro held under pace.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Big, close. Flick lands direct. Pace.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Fixed triangle. Chain, rhythm, straight.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Wide wall, rushed. Big flick, no pause.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Wide angles. Big flick, next in peripheral.
families.why: Original authored static circuit.

families.focus: Hold the pace as the targets multiply.
families.why: EvoClick adds a target every twenty seconds, so a run opens as a calm static read and ends as a crowded wall: a pacing arc no other static circuit here has. Community Benchmarks' easy cut leads into Revosect's three EvoClick tiers. The first cross-author handover needs playtesting.

families.focus: Pick your route through the gallery.
families.why: Vox's shooting-gallery layout offers route choice and quick successive kills. These Viscose click variants remove awkward spawns; Entry, Easier, Medium and Hard give the gallery a four-band progression.

families.focus: Chain the clears. Keep the rhythm alive.
families.why: Six-target reload clicking emphasizes a continuous clear-and-respawn rhythm. The first three cuts reduce target size; the Expert trustechain edit adds a different routing challenge. That final handover is a design choice requiring playtesting.

families.focus: Find a three-target beat and build speed.
families.why: Three close static targets create short, repeatable chains with little travel time. Larger 80%, Larger, standard and 10% small provide a size progression for a compact score-chasing circuit.
